name: screen_lua_states

ownership.argument: Firmware-owned table of borrowed lua_State pointers; Canopus only clears the slot that holds the calling interpreter's own state.

provenance.source: exact 4.100.179 vela_ap.bin: the literal pool of luaopen_screen (the function logging 'multiple miwear lua instances detected') holds this table and screen_state_cb 0xc6d1dfd. luaopen_screen stores its lua_State in the first free slot and registers screen_state_cb once; screen_state_cb calls lua_getglobal(L, "ScreenStateChangedCB") on every non-null slot at each screen change; only lua_module_miwear_close (the app framework's own Lua close) clears a slot.

notes: The NSH `lua` interpreter opens the miwear libraries, so every `lua` process (boot.lua at a pinned start, test drivers) leaves its freed state here when it exits. boot.lua clears its own slot (matched against tostring(coroutine.running())) with one aligned `mw` word write before anything else. Same code as 4.100.155 (exact IDB: luaopen_screen 0x0c6d1eb0, lua_module_miwear_close 0x0c8ea6a0); not run. Static evidence, device NOT_PROBED.
